question.text: In the classic LBO structure described in Chapter 8, what is the role of the 'acquisition company' (SPV)?

answer.text: It is the target investee company whose shares are being acquired
It is the custodian that safekeeps the acquisition proceeds
It is the sponsor entity of the AIF at the offshore level
It is a special-purpose acquisition vehicle that pools debt and equity and acquires control of the target, ring-fencing debt providers

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 8.3.1.2 describes the acquisition company as an SPV set up to pool both equity (from PE) and debt (senior/sub/mezzanine) and execute the takeover, giving debt providers a ring-fenced, secured claim. It is not the target. **The Trap:** Option A reverses the structure. Option C confuses it with the sponsor of the AIF itself. Option D mixes it with custodian role from Section 7 ecosystem. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests LBO/SPV mechanics; III-A/C (Compliance) test the related disclosure obligations for take-private. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In an LBO SPV, insist on step-up covenants and cash-sweep clauses in the debt docs — they force deleveraging in boom years and protect the equity upside at exit.
